issues.legal_issue: The dharamshala formed part of the math endowment rather than a separate endowment.
material_facts: The math and dharamshalas were supported by a grant whose produce was used to feed ascetics and visitors at both locations.
The dharamshalas and math property had historically been managed and dealt with together as one unit.
Earlier litigation concerning the math treated the dharamshala as part of the math property.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent finding that the dharamshala was part of the math endowment was supported by adequate evidence and was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The court considered the purpose and historical administration of the endowment, including that feeding disciples, travellers, and ascetics was an integral duty of a mahant. It referred to the dedication of a math described in the Varaha Purana, as quoted in Dr. Mukherjea's Hindu Law of Religious and Charitable Trusts.

rule.if: religious_endowment_identity_dispute and (common_endowment_funding and common_management and prior_treatment_as_one_property)

predicates.religious_endowment_identity_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether property associated with a religious institution belongs to its endowment or is a separate endowment.
predicates.common_endowment_funding: The institution's grant or other endowment resources were used to maintain both the institution and the associated property.
predicates.common_management: The institution and the associated property were historically managed and dealt with together.
predicates.prior_treatment_as_one_property: Earlier dealings or litigation treated the institution and the associated property as a single unit.

issues.definition: When an endowment-identity dispute concerns associated property that shares the institution's funding and management and was previously treated as one unit, the property is part of the institution's endowment.

issues.legal_issue: A mahant's borrowing to defend the rightful control and possession of math property may be a necessary expense of the math.
material_facts: Earlier litigation concerned competing claims to the office of mahant and the possession of the math's property.
The debts for which the later mortgage was given included expenses incurred in that litigation.
The litigation concerned whether the rightful mahant could control and possess property belonging to the math.
Succeeding mahants did not challenge the mortgage, and the sect's leading body treated the litigation expenses as a legitimate charge on the math property.
issues.conclusion: The mortgage was supported by legal necessity because the litigation expenses were incurred to repel a hostile attack on the trust property.
issues.legal_principle: A mahant's power to charge math property is limited to necessity or benefit to the endowment. Litigation to establish the rightful mahant's control and possession of endowed property can defend the math itself, rather than merely vindicate a personal claim. The court relied on Murugesam Pillai v. Manickavasaka Pandara, which recognizes the evidentiary weight of successive heads of an institution recognizing and dealing with a debt as an institutional debt.

rule.if: math_property_mortgage_dispute and litigation_expenses_incurred and litigation_defended_rightful_control_of_endowment_property and (successive_heads_recognized_debt or institutional_authority_treated_debt_as_legitimate)

predicates.math_property_mortgage_dispute: The proceeding concerns a mortgage of property belonging to a religious institution.
predicates.litigation_expenses_incurred: The institution's head borrowed money to pay expenses of litigation.
predicates.litigation_defended_rightful_control_of_: The litigation addressed a hostile claim that kept the rightful head from control or possession of property belonging to the institution.
predicates.successive_heads_recognized_debt: Successive heads of the institution accepted or dealt with the debt as an institutional obligation.
predicates.institutional_authority_treated_debt_as_: An authority representing the institution or its religious community treated the litigation debt as a legitimate charge on institutional property.

issues.definition: When a mortgage dispute concerns institutional property, the borrowing paid for litigation defending the rightful head's control of that property, and the debt was recognized by successive heads or institutional authority, the mortgage is supported by legal necessity.

issues.legal_issue: An alienation of part of a religious endowment to discharge an established debt and preserve the remaining property may be supported by legal necessity and benefit to the estate.
material_facts: A decree for a debt secured by a mortgage had led to an auction sale of nearly all of the dharamshala, and the creditor had obtained possession.
The High Court allowed the sale to be set aside if the judgment debtors deposited the amount due by a set deadline.
The creditor refused to accept a smaller portion of the property for the amount due.
The mahant and a committee of trustees arranged for buyers to purchase a much smaller portion for that amount, allowing the rest of the property to be saved for the math.
The sale deed recited that the transaction protected the math from losing the entire building.
issues.conclusion: The sale was supported by legal necessity and was valid because, without it, the portion of the property that the sale preserved would have been lost to the trust.
issues.legal_principle: In assessing necessity, the court considered the actual pressure on the estate, the immediate danger to be averted, and the benefit to be conferred. A manager may charge endowed property where there is necessity or benefit to the estate; the court relied on Prosunno Kumari Debya v. Golab Chand Baboo, Hunooman Persaud Panday v. Mt. Babooee Mundraj Koonweree, and Niladri Sahu v. Mahant Chaturbhuj Das. The relevant inquiry is the immediate pressure or benefit, even where earlier events contributed to the debt.

predicates.religious_endowment_alienation_dispute: The proceeding concerns an alienation of property belonging to a religious endowment.
predicates.enforceable_debt_threatened_endowment_pr: An enforceable debt exposed the endowment's property to loss through execution or another collection process.
predicates.payment_would_prevent_loss_of_property: Paying the debt would avert the threatened loss of endowment property.
predicates.sale_of_limited_property_would_preserve_: A sale of a limited portion of the endowment's property would discharge the debt and preserve the remainder from loss.

issues.definition: When an enforceable debt threatens endowment property and payment or a limited sale would avert that loss or preserve the remainder, the alienation is supported by legal necessity.

issues.legal_issue: The compromise disposal of the earlier suit did not operate as res judicata to bar the later suit.
material_facts: An earlier suit sought a declaration that the dharamshala was wakf property and challenged the effect of an auction sale.
One plaintiff withdrew from that suit after becoming mahant, and the remaining plaintiffs stated that the suit had been compromised.
The earlier suit was dismissed following that compromise, and the later suit challenged the subsequent sale and the status of the property.
issues.conclusion: The earlier suit did not operate as res judicata, and the Supreme Court upheld the High Court's determination on that issue.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and upheld the High Court's conclusion that the disposition of the earlier suit did not create a res judicata bar. The judgment states that it did so for the reasons given by the High Court, without setting those reasons out further.

predicates.later_suit_res_judicata_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether an earlier suit bars a later suit concerning the property or transaction.
predicates.prior_suit_ended_after_compromise: The earlier suit was dismissed after the remaining plaintiffs stated that it had been compromised.

issues.definition: When a later suit raises a res judicata dispute and the earlier suit ended after a compromise, the earlier suit does not bar the later suit.
